source_evidence: Typically, you pay a broker a fee called a commission or markup every time you buy or sell an investment. Typically you pay an adviser an ongoing asset-based fee based on the total value of your account.
question: How do transaction-based fees differ from asset-based fees in a client relationship summary?
answer: A transaction-based fee is typically a commission or markup paid each time you buy or sell an investment. An asset-based fee is typically an ongoing fee based on the total value of your account. The fees you pay depend on your agreement, and other fees or costs may also apply.
